title: Extend a Guardrail — Add a Label
note: There is ONE syntax for `classifiers` — LEDGER POSITION alone decides whether an entry declares or refines. The first entry for a namespace is the base; every later entry is a tighten-only overlay. Labels are the only additive direction, and even there the additivity is one-way: an overlay may ADD a label the base does not define, and may NEVER redefine or remove one. That restriction is not fussiness — a label name is a wire value a stranger's agent has already read and acted on, so removing it would strand them and redefining it would silently change what their past decisions meant. A collision with the base or with any earlier overlay is refused loudly rather than merged. The only path to changing an existing label is a NEW BASE VERSION of the whole vocabulary, which a verifier can see and pin. Labels are capped at 64 per namespace, which is why this vocabulary is sixteen families rather than one list. Note this family is UNSEALED and so accepts additive overlays; the six sealed families (authority, consent, safety, injection, disclosure, human-loop) refuse even this.
